title: §4.2 belt-and-braces guard is never executed in the request path — only tests call it
evidence: Doc comment: "this re-verifies the serialized payload can never carry the internal-only markers, whatever the stored row contains (a spoofed/malformed payload can't leak internals)." then `pub fn verify_payload_has_no_internal_fields(payload: String) -> Bool {`. handle_get_detail (hunk @@ -124,6 +125,27 @@) calls only `sql.list_reference_calls_for_detail` + `encode_reference_call`; the only call site in the diff is the test: `application_detail_handler.verify_payload_has_no_internal_fields(wire)`.
detail: The documented runtime re-verification never runs on the real payload. Cleanliness rests solely on the SQL strip + encoder whitelist; if the read drifts, no production backstop exists — only the integration test would catch it.
recommended_fix: Invoke the guard on the built body in handle_get_detail (fail the response or log loudly), or downgrade the doc comment to state it is test-only enforcement.

title: Guard checks escaped wire forms for referee_ip/referee_user_agent only — form_token/payload_ref escaped forms unchecked
evidence: `let markers = [ "\"form_token\"", "\"payload_ref\"", "\"referee_ip\"", "\"referee_user_agent\"", "\\\"referee_ip\\\"", "\\\"referee_user_agent\\\"", ]` and the comment: "both forms are checked so the guard can't be beaten by the escaping (Perkins-style lens finding, rc4-1 self-review #1)."
detail: Any key inside the result JSON-string field appears backslash-escaped on the wire; the SQL strip deletes only the two form_session paths, so a result doc carrying a form_token/payload_ref key at any other path reaches the wire escaped and the guard returns clean. Self-review #1's fix covers 2 of 4 markers.
recommended_fix: Add `\"form_token\"` and `\"payload_ref\"` to the marker list (and pin them in verify_payload_guard_detects_internal_markers_test, which currently feeds only escaped referee_ip).

title: next_attempt_at wire format is timestamptz::text ("2026-08-01 09:00:00+00") — not the ISO T/Z form fixtures and attempts[].at use
evidence: `COALESCE(next_attempt_at::text, '') AS next_attempt_at,` while the unit fixture uses `next_attempt_at: "2026-08-01T09:00:00Z"` and the attempt log stores ISO: `[{\"at\":\"2026-08-01T08:00:00Z\",...}]`.
detail: timestamptz::text renders space-separated with a session-timezone offset (verified: 2026-08-01 09:00:00+00), so the same §8.1 entry carries two datetime formats and the offset shifts if the DB session TZ is not UTC. Fixture implies ISO-T was intended.
recommended_fix: Select to_char(next_attempt_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS"Z"') (or NULLIF) so the wire matches the ISO form the fixtures/attempt log use.

title: Unknown outcome serializes as terminal "unreachable" while hooks (status-derived) can still say recordable
evidence: `outcome: case row.outcome { "" -> None; s -> Some(shared_reference_call.outcome_from_string(s)) }` and the pinned fallback: `reference_call.outcome_from_string("some_future_value") |> should.equal(OutcomeUnreachable)`.
detail: Self-review #3 made unknown status and hooks agree (both fail to failed), but an unknown outcome renders "unreachable" — a terminal outcome — on a row whose hooks say can_record_manual: true. Wire and hooks diverge exactly as #3 claimed to prevent.
recommended_fix: Map unknown outcome strings to None (omit) instead of OutcomeUnreachable, or document why a terminal-looking outcome may appear on a recordable row.

title: display_disclaimer fires on any object at verification — an empty {} block yields "provenance-checked"
evidence: Comment: "The verification block is an OBJECT when a written response exists; it is null on minimal terminal results... require a dict to distinguish 'a response exists' from 'no response'." Code: `case decode.run(value, decode.at(["verification"], decode.dict(decode.string, decode.dynamic))) { Ok(_) -> Some(written_response_disclaimer)`.
detail: The check is key-presence, not content: verification:{} or an all-null block emits the "provenance-checked" note with nothing checked, contradicting the comment's response-exists distinction and the disclaimer's provenance claim.
recommended_fix: Require at least one non-null verification field (e.g. decode non-null identity_confirmed) before emitting the disclaimer, and add a verification:{} unit test.
